title: Surgical account saves playbook
summary: A compact, action-first playbook for fast, targeted interventions on accounts showing mid-to-high renewal risk. Emphasizes quick hypothesis-driven experiments, exec-level escalation templates, and a lightweight scoring rubric to convert risk signals into a coordinated, time-boxed rescue plan.
body:
Purpose:
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction process for Customer Success Managers (CSMs) and their partners to triage, escalate, and execute ‘surgical’ save plays for accounts at risk of non-renewal.

When to use this doc:
- Account shows 2+ negative renewal signals within 30 days (usage drop, support spikes, missed QBR commitments, billing disputes).
- Account tier = mid/enterprise and/or contract value > $50k ARR and behavior deviates from baseline.
- Pre-QBR runway: 60–90 days from renewal where mitigation still has measurable impact.

Quick-read scoring (single-line):
- Score 0–6 (0 = healthy, 6 = critical) computed by adding:
  - Usage drop (>40% month-over-month): +2
  - Support severity incidents (P0/P1): +2
  - Executive disengagement (missed SLAs/meetings): +1
  - Contract/negotiation friction (billing/legal requests): +1
  - Product/quality regression called out in customer tickets: +1

Triage buckets and recommended cadence:
- Score 0–1: Watch (weekly check-ins, monitor dashboards)
- Score 2–3: Tactical outreach (CSM-led 1:1, targeted play within 14 days)
- Score 4: Rapid save (cross-functional warroom, 7-day sprint)
- Score 5–6: Exec escalation (Eng + Product + Sales + CS sync, daily updates until stabilized)

Surgical playbook matrix (by primary issue vector):
- Adoption/Usage drop:
  - Hypothesis: onboarding/training gap, rollout stalled, feature not adopted.
  - Immediate actions: schedule targeted onboarding lab with power-users (30–45 min), share success playbook from similar accounts, enable usage tracking tags.
  - KPIs to watch: weekly DAU/seat, feature-specific events, support asking rate.
- Quality/regression:
  - Hypothesis: a recent release caused regressions or degraded UX.
  - Immediate actions: 1) Open a joint incident with SRE/serving-runtime; 2) Request telemetry extraction for the customer's error spikes; 3) Offer a compensatory sandbox/rollback plan.
  - KPIs: error rate, time-to-first-fix, customer sentiment score post-fix.
- Contract/billing friction:
  - Hypothesis: invoice mismatch or pricing objections.
  - Immediate actions: finance + CSM alignment call, provide one-off credit or clearly scoped discount path, create transparent timeline for resolution.
  - KPIs: dispute resolution time, invoiced vs agreed amount, legal touchpoints.
- Executive disengagement:
  - Hypothesis: stakeholder priorities shifted, sponsor turnover.
  - Immediate actions: capture ‘what success looks like’ in one page, request a 15-minute sponsor check-in, prep exec briefing that quantifies business impact of going dark.
  - KPIs: meeting acceptance rate, sponsor action items closed.

7-day rapid-save sprint template (use when score >=4):
Day 0 (kickoff): CSM opens warroom, invites Eng lead, Product PM, Sales AE, Finance rep; agree on objective and 3 success metrics.
Day 1–2: Discovery and evidence collection (logs, usage, ticket timeline, contract history).
Day 3–4: Run 2–3 small experiments (e.g., targeted enablement, quick rollback, invoice correction, executive intro).
Day 5: Evaluate experiments, choose the winning move.
Day 6–7: Execute the fix and draft customer-facing summary.
Timeline rules: all actions should have an owner, ETA, and visible status in the shared warroom doc (linked artifact).

Exec escalation packet (one-pager to send to execs):
- Subject line template: "[Action requested] Save: <Account name> — Risk Score <X> — <ARR>"
- One-line ask: 2–3 line summary of help required (e.g., urgent rollback, exec intro to sponsor, approval for one-time credit).
- Impact: ARR at risk, 12-month revenue delta, product/brand risk.
- Proposed next steps with owners and ETA.
- Attachments: short timeline, evidence (tickets/graphs), customer quote.

Customer message templates (CSM -> Sponsor)
- Short re-engage (use for missed meetings): "Hi <Name>, noticed we missed our last sync. We’ve identified a focused set of actions that should take ~1 week to validate and avoid disruption to your rollout. Can you spare 15 minutes Wednesday?"
- Post-fix summary: "Thanks for the sync — summary of actions, results, and next steps. We’ll follow-up on X date with the adoption plan."

Decision authority and spend limits:
- CSM: can approve credits up to $2k and run tactical experiments.
- AC (Account Champion / Sales): authorize up to $25k in one-off concessions after manager signoff.
- Revenue Ops/Finance: required for contract amendments or multi-month credits.

Warroom checklist (first 24 hours):
- Create shared Google sheet (columns below) and add to warroom folder.
- Add telemetry snapshot, ticket exports, and recent webinar/QBR slides.
- Identify primary sponsor and escalation path.
- Assign owner for customer comms within 2 hours.

Recommended tracking sheet columns (minimal):
- account_name, tier, ARR, renewal_date, risk_score, primary_issue_vector, warroom_owner, exec_escalated (yes/no), actions (short list), next_eta, current_status, notes_link, last_touch_date

Sample short case log (informal):
- 2025-10-14: Usage down 55% after v3.2 deploy. Tickets x12 with elevated errors. CSM opens warroom.
- 2025-10-15: Eng confirms regression in tensor-kernel path; rollback scheduled.
- 2025-10-16: Rollback completed; user sessions returned to baseline; CSM scheduled sponsor call and applied $2k credit.

Playbook experiments (fast tests we recommend):
- Enable a temporary feature-flag revert for the account only.
- Offer a 30-minute customized enablement lab focused on the exact workflow that dropped.
- Apply a small one-time credit as a goodwill gesture to remove billing friction.
- Route traffic to a compatible model variant or lower-latency region as a short-term fallback.

Runbook for post-save (stabilize -> grow):
- T+0–14 days: Monitor usage, ticket volume and NPS for the account.
- T+15–45 days: Run adoption campaign (in-product tips, success stories, targeted enablement).
- T+45–90 days: Prepare QBR focusing on regained value and next milestones; show data-driven ROI to sponsor.

Play rehearsal and readiness (CS team):
- Quarterly tabletop: pick 2 high-risk accounts as simulation seeds; run through the 7-day sprint in a practice warroom (non-customer).
- Pre-QBR dry-run: for accounts with renewal <90 days, CSMs should run a 15-min internal check using the scoring rubric.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Define which telemetry signals are fed automatically into scorecard (eng + product follow-up).
- Add a lightweight Slack alert integration to auto-create a warroom when score >=4.
- Create a one-click exec email template in Salesforce for faster ask.

Appendix: quick resources
- Links (searchable warroom templates, exec email drafts, sample billing credit form) — see linked_artifacts above.
- Roles: list of recommended on-call responders: Product PM (rotation), Eng lead (serving-runtime on-call), SRE (incident management), Finance (invoicing).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep language tight — execs want one metric and one ask.
- Avoid overuse of blanket discounts; prefer targeted experiments that move the needle.
- This doc intentionally stays compact so CSMs can snapshot and escalate within 30 minutes.

Version history:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Marisol)
- 2025-12-05: added rapid-save sprint template (Leah)
- 2026-02-15: tightened scoring rubric and exec packet (Omar)
